title: LGV–Vandermonde Bridge: Combinatorial Proof and Path Matrix Connection

problemStatement.formal: C(m+n, r) = Σ_k C(m,k)·C(n,r-k) proved via Finset.powersetCard partition (LGV non-crossing contribution); lgvDet2 2×2 path matrix determinant defined; vandermonde_chu_from_lgv connects sequential LGV to Chu identity
problemStatement.plain: Connect the Lindström–Gessel–Viennot (LGV) lemma to Vandermonde-type identities. The standard Vandermonde identity C(m+n,r) = Σ_k C(m,k)·C(n,r-k) is the single-path degenerate case of LGV applied to Bool-vector lattice paths, where the 'non-crossing' condition holds trivially since there is only one path.
whyMatters: Provides a combinatorial interpretation of Vandermonde via the LGV partition principle
Establishes the 2×2 LGV path matrix and its determinant formula for lattice paths
Identifies both standard Vandermonde (Bool-vector model) and Chu-Vandermonde (LGV e-function model) as instances of the same LGV framework
Creates infrastructure connecting ballot problem results (BallotProblemOQ03) to binomial identities
